data.description:
## Description

**What**: Implement the full orchestration replacing bash: `classifier.py` (pure-function tier selection), `findings.py` (single JSON normalization replacing the 5+ inline `python3` heredocs), and `dispatch.py` (`asyncio.gather` with `return_exceptions=True` for parallel specialists + overlays, with a partial-failure path that produces an explicit error entry on the PR for any failed specialist instead of aborting the entire review). Reduce `ci-llm-review-runner.sh` to a ≤50-line shim and delete `llm-api-call.sh`.

**Why**: SC1 and SC4 of the epic. This is the orchestration migration — the moment the bash runner stops driving the review pipeline and the Python module takes over. The partial-failure improvement is a user-observable improvement vs. the current bash runner (which aborts the whole review on a single transient provider error), but it is also a contract change for the review gate that needs explicit coordination with `record-review.sh` and `pre-commit-review-gate.sh`.

**Scope**:
- IN: `classifier.py` (pure-function tier selection mirroring existing classifier logic); `findings.py` (single JSON normalization implementation replacing all 5+ inline heredocs); `dispatch.py` with `asyncio.gather(return_exceptions=True)` and per-task error capture into findings (explicit error entry per failed specialist); `ci-llm-review-runner.sh` reduced to ≤50 lines (resolves `_PLUGIN_ROOT`, execs `python3 -m dso_ci_review.runner`); `llm-api-call.sh` deleted; CLI invocation contract test exercising every known caller's argument pattern.
- OUT: Provider implementations (S2); parity test job (S4); unit / integration tests beyond contract test (S5); doc updates (S6); cleanup at epic close (S7).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, the full review pipeline runs through the Python module end-to-end: `classifier.py` selects tier, `dispatch.py` runs parallel specialists + overlays via `asyncio.gather(return_exceptions=True)`, and `findings.py` normalizes the output into the `reviewer-findings.json` schema.
  ← Satisfies: "New `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/` Python package replaces bash orchestration"
- When this story is complete, `ci-llm-review-runner.sh` is a ≤50-line shim that resolves `_PLUGIN_ROOT` and execs `python3 -m dso_ci_review.runner`, AND the shim preserves the exact argv contract, environment-variable contract, exit-code contract, and stdout/stderr contract of the previous bash runner. The contract is documented in the shim and a contract test invokes the shim with each known caller's argument pattern (CI workflow, /dso:review skill dispatch, any direct invocations enumerated in S2.5) asserting the same observable behavior.
  ← Satisfies: "ci-llm-review-runner.sh reduced to ≤50 lines and exists only as a thin shim"
- When this story is complete, `llm-api-call.sh` is deleted from the repo.
  ← Satisfies: "llm-api-call.sh deleted"
- When this story is complete, `dispatch.py` uses `asyncio.gather(return_exceptions=True)` AND on any provider call failure (5xx-class error, network failure, timeout) the review degrades to partial findings instead of aborting the whole run, with an explicit error entry per failed specialist surfaced in the PR review summary. Verified by a test that injects a 5xx-class error into one specialist call and asserts the resulting `reviewer-findings.json` includes (a) the surviving specialists' findings and (b) an explicit error entry for the failed specialist.
  ← Satisfies: "asyncio.gather partial-failure handling produces a user-observable improvement vs. the current bash behavior"

## Considerations

- [Performance] `asyncio.gather` MUST use `return_exceptions=True` with per-task error capture into findings — without this, one provider error cancels sibling tasks and the partial-failure SC is unmet.
- [Reliability] Shim ↔ Python entry-point PATH/venv mismatch is a known deployment risk on CI runners with multiple python3s. The shim resolves the package path explicitly and the CI install step uses `actions/setup-python` with cached pip and an editable install (`pip install -e .`) before the runner is invoked.
- [Security] Switching from run-abort to partial-degradation is a contract change for the review gate. The current bash runner aborts the entire review on a single specialist failure (fail-closed). The new behavior degrades to partial findings + error entry — fail-open for transient provider failures. Verify that `pre-commit-review-gate.sh` and `record-review.sh` accept partial findings.json with error entries as a valid review artifact OR explicitly mark partial reviews as non-passing via a new field. Without this verification, a missing specialist that would have flagged a critical finding could silently let bad code through.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a maintainer, full CI review orchestration runs through the Python module with partial-failure handling and a contract-preserving shim
